milestone_name: STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P5 -- controlled HOT/COLD production cutover and main-DB rebuild
status: DESIGN ONLY -- no P5 action taken in P4, per explicit instruction. Requires SEPARATE human authorization before any step below is executed.
prerequisites_from_p4: exact dbstat byte-level measurement of transfer_index (deferred twice now, P3 and P4, both times due to competing production load -- must be obtained in a genuine idle/maintenance window before P5 sizing is finalized)
segment discovery index implementation (Part 13, not yet built)
at least one real production-scale (not fixture-scale) archival dry-run to validate the keyset cursor's throughput against the actual 5.2M-row table

wiring UnifiedTransferReader into the 1 ADAPTER_REQUIRED consumer identified in the census (main.py's /api/transfer-graph/stats) and observing it in production for a period before trusting it as the sole read path

sequence.1_archival_high_water: freeze a run_id + high_water_id using start_or_resume_run() against the LIVE transfer_index, at a chosen production-quiet time
sequence.2_cold_segment_creation: run_keyset_archival() to copy all eligible (non-pinned, older-than-90-days) rows up to the frozen high-water into monthly COLD segments, using the already-tested keyset cursor -- copy-only, zero source mutation
sequence.3_validation: verify each segment's row count, signature digest, and manifest against the source query that produced it; run the full query-parity test suite (Part 14-18 mechanics) against REAL migrated data, not just fixtures
sequence.4_replacement_main_db_construction: build a new main DB file containing all non-transfer_index tables unchanged, plus ONLY the PERMANENT_PINNED + RECENT_GENERIC_HOT transfer_index subset (per the exact pinning contract, Part 3-4 of this milestone)
sequence.5_application_read_cutover: point read call sites at the new DB + COLD segments via UnifiedTransferReader; keep the OLD main DB available as a live fallback during a defined observation window
sequence.6_writer_cutover: point the actual write path (transfer_indexer.py, confirmed as the writer in this milestone's census) at the NEW main DB -- this is the point of no return for new data and must be carefully sequenced with step 5
sequence.7_brief_maintenance_window: a short window is likely unavoidable around steps 5-6 to avoid a split-brain state where new writes land in the old DB after reads have already cut over -- exact duration to be measured in a P5 dry run, not guessed here
sequence.8_rollback: OLD MAIN DB retained read-only (quarantined, not deleted) for a defined observation period; rollback = repoint reads+writes back to the old DB, no COLD reconstruction needed since old DB still has 100% of pre-cutover data
sequence.9_old_db_quarantine: old DB moved to a clearly-marked quarantine path (following the same _retired/ pattern already proven safe in STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P2 Part 1), read-only, retained until observation passes
sequence.10_observation: monitor query correctness, latency, error rates, and absence of HOT_COLD_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT surges for a defined period (recommend >=7 days minimum, informed by the existing 48-72h precedent from P2.2 but likely longer given this is a much higher-stakes cutover)
sequence.11_eventual_old_db_retirement: only after observation passes AND an explicit separate human decision -- never automatic

rollback_contract.no_reconstruction_from_cold_required: the OLD main DB, quarantined but intact, IS the complete rollback target -- COLD segments exist for forward capacity/growth management, not as the rollback mechanism
rollback_contract.no_immediate_deletion_after_cutover: explicit requirement carried forward from the human directive -- old DB deletion is a SEPARATE future decision after successful observation, never bundled into the cutover itself

lock_safety_carried_forward: SQLITE_STORAGE_LIFECYCLE_LOCK_SAFETY applies throughout: bounded batches (proven in P4's keyset cursor), no long write transaction on the live DB during archival (copy-only), cold writes isolated to their own files, busy-source handling (P1's DatabaseBusyError skip/continue pattern) reused rather than reinvented.
not_authorized_by_this_artifact: This document is a DESIGN ONLY. No step in the sequence above is executed by STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P4. P5 requires its own separate milestone directive with its own explicit human GO decision.
